land.text: the Thuringian kingdom conquered by the Franks in 531-532

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's kingdom row ends in 533 and the land sits inside the Frankish shape in 534-566; the Duchy row restarts the same shape in 567.

land.text: the whole duchy, ruled by Frankish dukes after Charles Martel

successors.note: c. 719 ('around 717-19 brought an end to autonomy'); Cliopatria's Frankish shape takes the land only in 724.

capitals.name: Erfurt
capitals.note: The Duchy page's infobox names Erfurt as capital but the text names no early seat; Radulf's seat was 'a fortress on the Unstrut river' (Radulf page). The span is the researcher's reading.

capitals.name: Würzburg
capitals.note: 'In a donation dated 1 May 704 in Würzburg, his capital' (Hedan II page); the Thuringi page also puts the seat 'at Würzburg in the south' under Charles Martel.

rulers.name: Radulf
rulers.title: Duke (king of Thuringia from 642)
rulers.note: Ducal list 632-642; the Radulf page: duke 'before 632/633, until 641/642'.

rulers.name: Heden II
rulers.title: Duke
rulers.note: The Hedan II page makes him rule 'from around 700 until his death' in 741 and calls Würzburg his capital; the Duchy page's list ends in 719.

keyframe_review.note: 40,557 km2 (9.2-12.3E, 49.3-51.9N): Thuringia between the Harz, the Thuringian Forest, the Saale and the upper Main; the shape is the one Cliopatria gives the Kingdom of Thuringia (476-533) and, apart from one cell, every later Thuringian shape. The Duchy page gives no area. Status is the doubt: 'During the first half of the 6th century, Thuringia came under the supreme rule of Frankish kings' (battle on the Unstrut, 531), the Thuringi 'were placed under Frankish dukes, but they rebelled' (Thuringi page), and the duchy is 'established ... about 631, by King Dagobert I'. Cliopatria's Frankish shape holds this land in 534-566 and in 633-640 (173 cells) but not in 567-632, so the years 567-630 are a Cliopatria choice the pages do not support; kept as drawn (the land is then not blank) and flagged in the notes. Its east edge follows the Saale: 'The estates east of the Saale River were beyond Frankish control and taken over by Polabian Slavs'.

40,403 km2: the 567 shape minus one cell at 12.2E, 50.75N. Cliopatria's Thuringia returns in 641 after the 633-640 years inside the Franks' shape, which matches Radulf's revolt: 'About 641' Sigebert III marched against him, and 'In 642, he rebelled against Sigebert and defeated his army, taking the title of rex or king of Thuringia.' The Thuringi page speaks of independence 'regained by the late seventh century under Radulf' and of parts of Thuringia that 'came under Saxon rule' towards the end of the 7th century; neither changes the shape.

40,557 km2: the 641 shape plus the single cell. Heden I (642-687), Gozbert (687-689) and Heden II (689-719) on the Duchy page's ducal list; the Hedan II page puts Hedan's capital at Würzburg ('In a donation dated 1 May 704 in Würzburg, his capital') and a donation of 716/717 'on the Saale'. No border event on the pages opened.

40,557 km2, the same land to 723. 'A conflict with Charles Martel around 717-19 brought an end to autonomy' and the ducal list ends in 719; Cliopatria's Franks hold the land from 724 (171 cells), not in 718-723. The land is Frankish from 720, so the shape is cut to 718-719 and the Franks' shape, which lacks it in 720-723, must take it over (successor in the identity). The Hedan II page makes Hedan rule until 741; the pages disagree.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 718 shape unchanged, for 718-719 only; from 720 the land is Frankish ('A conflict with Charles Martel around 717-19 brought an end to autonomy').

region.text: Thuringia between the Harz, the Thuringian Forest, the Saale and the Main

ledger.note: 567: Thuringia, under Frankish supreme rule since the Unstrut campaign of 531, appears as a Thuringian duchy in Cliopatria. The year is Cliopatria's; the Duchy page says only that Thuringia 'came under the supreme rule of Frankish kings' in the first half of the 6th century.

c. 631: King Dagobert I establishes the duchy of Thuringia and installs Radulf as its duke. 'It was established as a duchy about 631, by King Dagobert I'; Radulf was 'installed by King Dagobert in the early 630s' (ducal list 632-642). Radulf holds the Saale frontier against the Wends.

region.text: Thuringia, drawn inside the Frankish shape in 633-640

ledger.note: 633: Cliopatria draws Thuringia as part of the Frankish kingdom for 633-640 (173 cells in the Frankish shape) while Radulf governs it as Dagobert's duke. The Duchy page is silent on any change in 633: bridging judgement from the Cliopatria shapes.

region.text: Thuringia, where Sigebert III's expedition marched against Radulf

ledger.note: c. 641: Radulf rebels against King Sigebert III. 'About 641' Sigebert III marched against Radulf and his ally Fara, the Agilolfing; Fara was routed, but Radulf held his fortress on the Unstrut. Duchy page, after Fredegar: he rebelled against King Sigebert III in 641/2; Samo page: 'In 641, the rebellious Radulf sought an alliance with Samo against his sovereign'.

region.text: the former Thuringian kingdom under Radulf

ledger.note: 641/2: Thuringia leaves direct Frankish rule under Radulf (Cliopatria's shape returns in 641). The page gives 'In 642' for the royal title and 'About 641' for the king's march; the whole former kingdom is the researcher's reading of 'the former Thuringian kingdom'.

642: Radulf takes the title of king of Thuringia. 'In 642, he rebelled against Sigebert and defeated his army, taking the title of rex or king of Thuringia.' His sons Theotbald and Heden I succeed him.

642: the Frankish expedition fails. Radulf was 'not overcome, partially because he had gained the support of significant numbers of the king's forces'; the Duchy page: the punitive expedition of the king and the mayor Grimoald 'failed'.

704: the ducal seat is at Würzburg on the Main. 'In a donation dated 1 May 704 in Würzburg, his capital', Hedan II grants Willibrord Arnstadt, Mühlberg and Großmonra; the Duchy page names no early seat and shows Erfurt only as the infobox capital.

c. 719: Charles Martel ends Thuringian autonomy. 'A conflict with Charles Martel around 717-19 brought an end to autonomy'; Heden II is the last duke on the list (689-719). Cliopatria keeps the shape to 723 and gives the land to the Franks in 724; the Hedan II page has Hedan rule to 741.

wars.name: Samo's Wends against Frankish Thuringia
wars.outcome: After Samo beat Dagobert I at Wogastisburg ('in 631 or 632') the Sorbs under Dervan joined him and he 'invaded Frankish Thuringia several times and undertook looting raids there'; Dervan's wars are dated 'successfully fighting against Frankish Thuringia (631-634)'.
wars.note: No border change is recorded: Radulf 'fought successfully against the Slavs' and held the Saale frontier (Radulf page). In 641 Radulf himself sought Samo's alliance.

wars.name: Radulf's revolt against Sigebert III
wars.outcome: Sigebert III's expedition failed (Fara's troops were routed and Fara killed, but Radulf held his fortress); in 642 Radulf defeated the king's army and took the title of king of Thuringia.
wars.note: The page does not give the site of the 642 battle; the Duchy page mentions no battle on the Unstrut in 641.

wars.name: Conflict with Charles Martel
wars.outcome: 'A conflict with Charles Martel around 717-19 brought an end to autonomy.'
wars.note: The pages give no campaign, battle or date inside the span; the Thuringi page adds that under Charles Martel and Boniface the Thuringi 'were again subject to the Franks and ruled by Frankish dukes, with their seat at Würzburg'.

certainty.note: No treaty line on the pages opened. The one named frontier is the Saale against the Polabian Slavs ('The estates east of the Saale River were beyond Frankish control'); the Harz and Saxon edge and the Main edge are approximate.

notes:
Duchy of Thuringia, 567-719 (4 Cliopatria shapes, 5 pages including the Samo page opened for the Avar dossier).
- All four Cliopatria shapes are the same 40,557 km2 outline as the Kingdom of Thuringia (476-533); the shape is a cell template, not a surveyed border.
- Status 531-641: the pages say Frankish supreme rule from 531 and Frankish dukes; the duchy dates from about 631 (Dagobert I). Cliopatria draws a Thuringian state for 567-632, the Franks for 633-640 and 534-566, and Thuringia again from 641. The 567-630 span is therefore unsupported by the pages; the dossier keeps it (confidence 1 found event) so the land is not blank, and a gap-filler should decide whether 567-640 is a Frankish dependency (vassal tint under kingdom-of-the-franks, event for eu-07) rather than a state.
- The Franks' Cliopatria shape is missing the Thuringian land in 720-723 and in 567-632 (it holds it 534-566, 633-640, 724+). The identity.successors hand-over at 719 is meant to cover 720-723.
- Dukes disagree: the Duchy page lists Heden II 689-719; the Hedan II page has Hedan II rule from about 700 to 741 from Würzburg, and calls the duchy 'the region around the river Main'. End year follows the Duchy page (719); Cliopatria's last year is 723. The Thuringi page says parts of Thuringia 'came under Saxon rule' towards the end of the 7th century (undated, not drawn).
- Pages that would not load: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radulf_(duke_of_Thuringia) (the article is at Radulf,_King_of_Thuringia) and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Thuringia (no such title; the Thuringi page was used instead).
- Not verified (page budget): the Frankish duchy years 531-631, the Saxon incursions, the Charles Martel campaign dates 717-719, Boniface's mission and the foundation of the diocese of Erfurt (742, Hedan II page).
- Counterparts needing dossiers: kingdom-of-thuringia (eu-06, Cliopatria row 476-533) and kingdom-of-the-franks (eu-07).
